validation.notes: Repaired packages/coding-agent/src/migrations.ts::migrateSessionsFromAgentRoot with a one-token fix: the destination-collision branch used `return`, which aborted the entire migration batch on the first name collision; it now uses `continue`, so only the colliding file is skipped and the batch keeps going. The regression loads the real TypeScript module through the read-only .prale-eval/subject.mjs harness (real node:fs/node:path, only getAgentDir faked) and builds an agentDir in which the colliding session is chosen as the FIRST legacy session in readdirSync order, so at least five migratable sessions are guaranteed to follow it in the same batch. Assertions cover: (1) every later legacy session leaves the agent root and lands, byte-identical, in its encoded cwd directory (--work-alpha-- style); (2) the colliding source and the pre-existing destination copy are both preserved unchanged (no overwrite, no deletion); (3) malformed JSON, blank first line and non-session headers are never touched; (4) the sessions/ directory set equals exactly the encoded cwds of the migrated sessions; (5) a second invocation is a byte-for-byte no-op snapshot diff, proving idempotency. Exit status is 0 with 5 assertions groups passing (a final console.log reports the outcome but no assertion is replaced by output). Negative control run: an isolated copy of the workspace layout with only the original `return` fault restored was replayed with the same script and failed with `AssertionError: collision aborted the batch: legacy session session-beta.jsonl was left in the agent root instead of migrating` (exit 1), then the fixed workspace re-ran green. No optional dependencies were needed: Node 24.14.0 built-in TypeScript stripping plus node:vm modules sufficed, no network and no npm install were used, and the script removes its own .prale-eval scratch directory in a finally block.
